# teal.picks R Package Development Guide

## Package Overview

`teal.picks` is part of the `teal` framework and provides the dataset, variable and value pickers used in `teal` modules.
It lets `teal` app developers declare which dataset, columns and values the app user can choose,
renders the matching inputs, and merges the selected data into an analysis-ready `teal_data` object with reproducible code.

## Development Context

It provides 3 main features to the framework:

- `picks` specification (`R/picks.R`): `picks()` holds `datasets()`, then optionally `variables()` and `values()`
  - each `pick` is `list(choices, selected)` with `multiple`, `fixed` and `ordered` attributes
  - `choices`/`selected` are eager (`character`/values) or delayed: `tidyselect` (including integer positions like the default `selected = 1L`) or predicates (the only delayed form in `values()`)
- Shiny modules (`R/module_picks.R`, `inst/badge-dropdown/`): `picks_ui()`/`picks_srv()` show one input per `pick` in a badge drop-down and return a `reactiveVal` of resolved `picks`
- Merging (`R/module_merge.R`): `merge_srv()` turns resolved `picks` into `dplyr` select/filter/join code run on the `teal_data`; `tm_merge()` is an example module

See `vignettes/teal-picks-in-teal.Rmd` and `vignettes/teal-picks-standalone-shiny.Rmd` for usage.

### Internals

- `resolver()` resolves each `pick` in order (`determine()` generic), passing the selected data on: `teal_data` → dataset → columns. An empty `selected` empties everything after it.
- `values()` resolve against the unique values of the selected column(s). Range inputs need `ranged()`; plain numeric vectors are discrete choices (`?picks` still describes `c(min, max)` ranges).
- In `picks_srv()`, a new selection resets the following elements to their defaults (`.resolve()`).
- Pickers commit only when the drop-down closes (`<element>-selected_open` set to `FALSE`). Inputs are redrawn only when `choices` change.
- `merge_srv()` orders datasets by `join_keys`, keeps primary and foreign keys, and suffixes duplicated columns with `_<dataname>`.

### Relationships with other packages

Direct dependencies:

- `teal.data`: provides `teal_data` and `join_keys` used by `merge_srv()` to determine the merge order and join columns.
  - Any issue with `join_keys` should be addressed in `teal.data`.
- `teal.code`: reproducible code (`eval_code()`/`within()`) for the select, filter and merge calls.
- `teal`: `tm_merge()` and `teal_transform_filter()` build `teal::module()`/`teal::teal_transform_module()` objects.
- `tidyselect`: dynamic `choices`/`selected` are evaluated with `tidyselect`.
- `teal.transform` is in `Suggests`; `as.picks()` converts `data_extract_spec`/`select_spec`/`filter_spec` to `picks` to ease the transition away from `teal.transform`. Code paths that use it must check `requireNamespace()` and tests must use `testthat::skip_if_not_installed()`.

Usage in other framework packages:

- `teal.modules.general`, `teal.modules.clinical`, `teal.modules.gtsummary` and `teal.goshawk`: modules accept `picks` arguments (e.g. `dist_var = teal.picks::picks(...)`), call `picks_ui()`/`picks_srv()` in their UI/server and `merge_srv()` to build the analysis dataset.
  - `teal.modules.general` keeps `picks` versions of modules next to the `data_extract_spec` versions (`tm_*_picks.R`).
- The exported `app_driver_*()` helpers are used by `shinytest2` tests of downstream module packages to read, set and check pickers.

### Workflows

- Before fixing an issue consider that this package is part of teal framework, so a bug that manifests in this package might have a different origin.
- Changes to the public API (`picks()`/`datasets()`/`variables()`/`values()` arguments, `picks_srv()` and `merge_srv()` return values, `app_driver_*()` helpers) can break downstream module packages and must be verified against them.
- Reproduce resolution without Shiny: `print(resolver(picks, data))`, where `data` can be a `teal_data`.
- In `testServer()`, commit a selection with `session$setInputs("<element>-selected" = ..., "<element>-selected_open" = FALSE)`.
- In `shinytest2`, badge inputs aren't bound until the badge is opened; use `app_driver_get_teal_picks_slot()`/`app_driver_set_teal_picks_slot()`.

### Debugging tips

- Errors in delayed `choices`/`selected` are swallowed: you only get the warning "None of the `choices/selected` ... Emptying choices...". Run the predicate or `tidyselect::eval_select()` on the data to see the error.
- One unknown column empties a `tidyselect` selection (use `tidyselect::any_of()`); unknown names in `character` choices are dropped silently.
- The `picks_delayed` warning at construction also fires for the default `selected = 1L`; tests use `suppressWarnings(classes = "picks_delayed")`.
- `no applicable method for 'join_keys<-' ... 'qenv.error'` means the merge code failed. Print it with `.merge_expr(.merge_summary_list(selectors, teal.data::join_keys(data), "anl"), "anl", join_fun, data)` and run it with `teal.code::eval_code()`.
- Merge code uses `%>%`, so run `library(dplyr)` in the `teal_data` first. `load_all()` hides this because `testthat` exports `%>%`.
- `merge_srv()` waits silently (`req()`) while any selector is `NULL`.
- Debug logs: `logger::log_threshold("DEBUG", namespace = "teal.picks")`.
